title: Start tracking
briefing: You've built a little website in ~/site, but it isn't under version control.
One bad edit and there's no way back.
Put it in git: turn the folder into a repository and make a first commit
tips: The rhythm is: git init → git add . → git commit -m "message".
`git status` after each step shows you what git thinks is going on.
objective: Turn ~/site into a git repository and commit all of its files in a first commit.
expert_objective: Put ~/site under git with an initial commit of everything.
hints: Go there and start a repo: `cd ~/site`, then `git init`.
Stage everything, then commit: `git add .`, then `git commit -m "initial commit"`.
`cd ~/site && git init && git add . && git commit -m "initial commit"`. `git status` should then say 'working tree clean'.
solution:
cd ~/site
git init
git add .
git commit -m "initial commit"
explanation: Every git project starts the same way: `git init` creates the repository, `git add` stages what you want to save, and `git commit` records a snapshot with a message. 'working tree clean' means everything is safely committed — your undo history has begun.
